# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_018_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 10

**1** Then she showed me a huge crowd approaching from a distance, and at their center walked a man of extraordinary stature — taller than the tower itself — with the bearing of a great estate-owner: a magnificent crown on his head, dressed in gleaming white robes. **2** His feet were shod in white; in his right hand he carried a sickle, in his left a shepherd's staff. He came and took his stand in front of the tower. **3** He gave orders for the stones to be brought and fitted into the building. Six builders and four others on his right received them and continued the work. **4** He then ordered the other stone-carriers to reject all their stones and throw them far from the tower. But not a single stone that was lying near the tower got rejected — they were all placed in the building because they were smooth and bright. **5** Many stones far away were rejected, though. He directed these to be sorted into separate piles — different groups for different stones. The twelve mountains, however, were not piled up; they were arranged in order of their different characters. **6** Once the stones were fitted in, the man called to me: "Come here, Hermas." I went up to him. "What do you want to know?" he asked. "Lord," I said, "I want to understand this whole vision — beginning to end. What do all the placed stones mean, and the rejected ones, and those thrown far away? And why isn't the building finished yet?"

---

*PNEUMA note: The sovereign figure with crown, sickle, and crook is the most majestic figure in the entire Shepherd. He combines Christ as King, Harvester (Rev 14), and Good Shepherd (John 10) in one image.*
